# Scheme-theoretic rational normal curves from rank-two alternating Toeplitz matrices

## Finding
For every integer \(n\ge4\) and every field \(k\), let \(R=k[x_1,\ldots,x_{n-1}]\), and define the \(n\)-by-\(n\) alternating Toeplitz matrix \(A\) with \(A_{ij}=x_{j-i}\) if \(0\le i<j<n\), \(A_{ji}=-A_{ij}\), and \(A_{ii}=0\). Let \(I_n\subset R\) be the ideal of all principal \(4\)-by-\(4\) Pfaffians.

**Theorem.** The scheme \(\operatorname{Proj}(R/I_n)\subset\mathbb P^{n-2}_k\) is a rational normal curve of degree \(n-2\). The ideal \(I_n\) is prime over every field, and already generated by the following \(\binom{n-2}{2}\) selected Pfaffians, indexed by \(2\le i\le j\le n-2\):
\[
Q_{ij}=x_1x_{j+1-i}-x_ix_j+x_{i-1}x_{j+1}.
\]
These form a minimal homogeneous generating set. Its Hilbert series is
\[
\operatorname{Hilb}_{R/I_n}(t)=\frac{1+(n-3)t}{(1-t)^2}.
\]
Moreover, the only nonzero graded Betti numbers of \(R/I_n\) beyond \(\beta_{0,0}=1\) are
\[
\beta_{r,r+1}=r\binom{n-2}{r+1},\qquad 1\le r\le n-3.
\]
In particular, the non-generic linear section of \(\operatorname{Gr}(2,n)\) by the alternating Toeplitz coefficient space is smooth, integral, projectively normal, and has no embedded or nonreduced Pfaffian structure, in every characteristic.

## Assumptions and scope
All ideals are homogeneous over an arbitrary field; geometric smoothness and integrality are asserted after passage to an algebraic closure as well. The rank-at-most-two condition for an alternating form means the vanishing of all \(4\)-by-\(4\) principal Pfaffians, including characteristic \(2\), where alternating means zero diagonal and skew-symmetry is interpreted by signs modulo \(2\). The projective case requires \(n\ge4\), and no claim concerns higher even ranks.

## Proof
Put \(d=n-2\). In \(k[a,b]\), define \(P_0=1\), \(P_1=b\), and \(P_{r+1}=bP_r-a^2P_{r-1}\) for \(r\ge1\). Each \(P_r\) is homogeneous of degree \(r\), with leading term \(b^r\) and lower terms divisible by \(a^2\). Consider
\[
\nu:\mathbb P^1_k\longrightarrow\mathbb P^d_k,\qquad
[a:b]\longmapsto[a^dP_0:a^{d-1}P_1:\cdots:P_d].
\]
(The coordinate indexed by \(x_{r+1}\) is \(a^{d-r}P_r\).) Relative to the standard degree-\(d\) Veronese monomial basis \(a^{d-r}b^r\), these coordinates differ by an invertible triangular linear map with diagonal entries \(1\), over every field. Hence the image \(C\) is a rational normal curve, and its saturated homogeneous prime ideal \(J\) is generated by quadrics.

**All Pfaffians vanish on \(C\).** This is a polynomial identity over \(\mathbb Z\), so one may verify it in characteristic zero before reducing coefficients. On the dense open subset \(a\ne0\) and away from the repeated-root discriminant, choose two distinct roots \(\lambda,\mu\) of \(z^2-(b/a)z+1\). They satisfy \(\lambda\mu=1\). The recurrence gives
\[
x_s=a^d\frac{\lambda^s-\mu^s}{\lambda-\mu}\quad(1\le s<n).
\]
Thus \(A_{ij}\) for \(i<j\) is a scalar multiple of \(\mu^i\lambda^j-\lambda^i\mu^j\), i.e. the entries of a decomposable alternating \(2\)-form. Its rank is at most \(2\), so every \(4\)-by-\(4\) Pfaffian vanishes on a dense set. The resulting polynomial identities have integer coefficients and therefore remain identities after reduction to any characteristic. This proves \(I_n\subseteq J\).

**Enough independent Pfaffians.** For \(2\le i\le j\le n-2\), the Pfaffian on rows and columns \(0,1,i,j+1\) equals \(Q_{ij}\) displayed above. Give \(x_s\) weight \(s\), separately from its ordinary polynomial degree. The highest-weight part of \(Q_{ij}\) is
\[
H_{ij}=x_{i-1}x_{j+1}-x_ix_j;
\]
the omitted term has weight \(j+2-i<i+j\). For each fixed weight \(i+j\), the \(H_{ij}\) are consecutive differences along the chain of quadratic monomials with that weight. These differences are linearly independent over every field: in a nonzero relation, take the smallest first index of a participating pair; its outer monomial cannot cancel. Distinct weight classes cannot cancel either. Consequently the \(\binom{n-2}{2}\) polynomials \(Q_{ij}\) are linearly independent in \(R_2\).

The space of degree-two forms in \(J\) has dimension
\[
\dim_k J_2=\binom{d+2}{2}-(2d+1)=\binom d2=\binom{n-2}{2},
\]
because the quadratic piece of the Veronese coordinate ring is the complete space of binary forms of degree \(2d\). Since \(I_{n,2}\subseteq J_2\) already contains this many independent forms, \(I_{n,2}=J_2\). The ideal of a rational normal curve is generated by quadrics (equivalently, by \(2\)-by-\(2\) minors of its \(2\)-by-\(d\) catalecticant). Every generating Pfaffian is quadratic, so \(I_n=J\), scheme-theoretically and over every field.

**Invariants.** The coordinate ring is the \(d\)-th Veronese subring \(\bigoplus_{m\ge0} k[a,b]_{dm}\). Therefore its degree-\(m\) Hilbert function is \(dm+1\) and its Hilbert series is \((1+(d-1)t)/(1-t)^2\). The standard Eagon--Northcott resolution of the \(2\)-by-\(2\) minors of the catalecticant has minimal ranks \(r\binom d{r+1}\) in homological degree \(r\), with shifts \(r+1\). These results yield the asserted Betti numbers and geometric properties.

## Verification
The standalone `skew_toeplitz_verify.py` is included in the package and uses only the Python standard library. Run `python3 skew_toeplitz_verify.py`. It constructs homogeneous parameter polynomials from the recurrence over the integers; checks every \(4\)-by-\(4\) Pfaffian vanishes identically in the parameters for \(4\le n\le10\); and checks exact rational linear independence of the selected \(\binom{n-2}{2}\) quadrics. The final output is `VERIFY_OK`. These bounded computations corroborate but do not substitute for the uniform proof.

## Relationship to prior work
The ambient rank-two alternating locus is the classical Plücker Grassmannian. Faenzi and Fania, *Skew-symmetric matrices and Palatini scrolls* (arXiv:0906.1875, first public June 10, 2009), study spaces of alternating matrices and associated general Pfaffian degeneracy/scroll constructions, not this Toeplitz linear section or its uniform prime quadratic ideal. Fisher, *The invariants of a genus one curve* (arXiv:math/0610318, first public October 10, 2006), discusses Pfaffian presentations of genus-one normal curves; those curves and their matrix coefficient spaces have different geometry. Standard rational-normal-curve theory supplies the catalecticant ideal and Betti numbers **after** the Toeplitz Pfaffian section has been identified with that curve. Neither these standard facts alone nor an alternating-matrix rank criterion automatically identifies this special linear section scheme-theoretically.

## Limitations
The claim is restricted to the rank-at-most-two alternating Toeplitz scheme; it does not describe its higher-rank analogues, real rank stratifications, or intersections with additional linear constraints. Earlier equivalences hidden in general structured-Pfaffian or Toeplitz literature remain a literature-risk; independent specialist review has not been performed.
